faq.a: No. The only export format is WAV, written manually in the browser. The page explains MP3 is unavailable because it needs an external encoder library; WAV is lossless and universally supported. You choose 16-bit PCM or 32-bit float, sample rate (keep original, 44100, 48000 or 22050 Hz) and mono/stereo output, and an estimated output size is shown before you download.

faq.q: What does Auto Silence Trim actually measure?
faq.a: It finds the single loudest sample (the peak) in the first channel, sets a threshold at the percentage of peak you choose (0.5–20%, default 2%), then walks in from the start and end until a sample exceeds that threshold. The selection is moved to those points. It trims leading and trailing silence only — it won't remove silent gaps in the middle.

faq.q: How do the export presets change the settings?
faq.a: Each preset sets bit depth, channels and fades at once: Voice note = 16-bit mono, normalised; Ringtone = 16-bit stereo with 0.1s fade-in and 0.3s fade-out; Podcast clip = 16-bit mono with gentle 0.2s fades; Music = 32-bit stereo, no normalise; Smallest file = 16-bit mono. Your export settings are also remembered between files so batch work isn't repetitive.

faq.q: How does Split into Segments work?
faq.a: Type split points in seconds, comma-separated (e.g. 5, 12.5, 30). Points outside the clip or that aren't numbers are ignored, the rest are sorted, and the tool cuts at 0 → each point → end, exporting every segment as its own WAV bundled into a ZIP via JSZip. Each segment gets the same fades, gain, normalise and channel settings you've chosen.
